items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: so we went away, you see, with Chinch and Ella B. Moore, and we traveled throughout the South.

ctx.x: So Mr. Shelton Brooks said, 'That was good; they like you, and you just go over there and rest. you know, and so that's what happened. Then the next thing I know, this lady, Ella B. Moore -- this is Tish Moore's partner -- she was -- a great singer, she was -- Nellie Letcher was her protege, you know.

items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: she was the one that invited me to go and rejoin the church

ctx.x: And that really is fun, you know, because you can get rebaptized, and also you can get a new (unintelligible) you see. It's called a new cornerstone. And it's a lovely mother woman -- a lady -- she got her son -- grown son (unintelligible). I don't know whether he has made her a grandparent yet. But she was the one that invited me to go and rejoin the church, you know, up there in Brooklyn on Putnam Street.
And I just called the mother Mrs. Rights, you know. And she said, well, you should go, you know. Said God is the one to get your degrees from, you know. So --
Did she have anything to do with you dancing at the Jazz Vespers?
